‘AI & I’: FABLE 5 UPENDS HOW WE BUILD

Today, we’re releasing a new episode of our podcast AI & I https://every.to/emails/click/136f006095268802530f927779a5f4d55a493840c0f1f77c950761a77b64df9e/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSG93IHRvIEdldCB0aGUgTW9zdCBPdXQgb2YgRmFibGUgNSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQyOTQsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL3BvZGNhc3QiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6OH0=. Dan Shipper https://every.to/emails/click/136f006095268802530f927779a5f4d55a493840c0f1f77c950761a77b64df9e/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSG93IHRvIEdldCB0aGUgTW9zdCBPdXQgb2YgRmFibGUgNSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQyOTQsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BkYW5zaGlwcGVyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjl9 sits down with Mike Krieger, the cofounder of Instagram and head of Anthropic Labs, to discuss what it feels like to build with Fable 5 https://every., a model powerful enough that it’s forcing him to rethink the very definition of productivity, engineering, and creative agency.

As someone who built one of the most popular consumer apps in the pre-GPT era and has had access to Fable 5 for months, Krieger has a rare vantage point on what the radical compression of the product development arc means for builders.

Watch on X https://every.to/emails/click/136f006095268802530f927779a5f4d55a493840c0f1f77c950761a77b64df9e/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSG93IHRvIEdldCB0aGUgTW9zdCBPdXQgb2YgRmFibGUgNSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQyOTQsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL3guY29tL2RhbnNoaXBwZXIvc3RhdHVzLzIwNjQ3NjE2NTQ3ODk2ODEyODEiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6MTF9 or YouTube https://every.to/emails/click/136f006095268802530f927779a5f4d55a493840c0f1f77c950761a77b64df9e/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSG93IHRvIEdldCB0aGUgTW9zdCBPdXQgb2YgRmFibGUgNSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQyOTQsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL3d3dy55b3V0dWJlLmNvbS93YXRjaD92PVhXcFRnQ3ZnWWFFIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjEyfQ==, or listen on Spotify https://every. or Apple Podcasts https://every._aT0xMDAwNzcyMDY3NjM3IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjE0fQ==. You can also read the transcript https://every..

Here are the highlights:

 1. More work is happening overnight. Fable 5 is the first model capable enough that you can hand it a complex task, walk away, and trust it will be completed by morning. When it hits an obstacle—a remote service goes down, say, or a tool stops working—it writes a workaround and forges ahead. That resilience has changed the daily rhythm of Krieger’s work: He now ends his workday by briefing the model on what needs to get done while he sleeps, rather than sitting down to do it himself.
 2. The gap between what’s in your head and what exists in the world is closing. Given access to Fable 5 and a set of internal MCPs, an Anthropic recruiter described the experience as, “The first time in my life where I feel like the thing that’s in my head and the thing that exists in the world are right next to each other. I can just do it.” This is the most meaningful thing about the new model class, Krieger says—it allows non-engineers to create the exact products they need to get more done.
 3. Software engineering is dead. Long live software engineering. Engineers now spend less time writing code and more time setting direction, reviewing what their AI agents have built, and making judgment calls when something breaks in production. The divide between product managers and engineers has blurred. “There is a feeling of loss, I think, in some of the better engineers that I talk to, as well as the feeling of, ‘Oh my God, but I can do insane amounts of work now at the same time.’ We’re holding both ideas in our heads at once,” Krieger says.
 4. All eyes are on verification. If we can delegate more to the model, it becomes more important to check what it has built works in practice. Krieger’s approach combines regression testing on known workflows, visual checks—including giving the model video captures of its own work so it can catch animation glitches screenshots would miss—and mock backends for anything too complex to test live. When a bug arrives via Slack, Fable 5 makes the fix, posts the pull request, then follows up hours later.

HOW THE EVERY TEAM IS USING FABLE 5

The easiest way to be disappointed by Fable 5 is to use it as if it were GPT-5.5 https://every.to/emails/click/136f006095268802530f927779a5f4d55a493840c0f1f77c950761a77b64df9e/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSG93IHRvIEdldCB0aGUgTW9zdCBPdXQgb2YgRmFibGUgNSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQyOTQsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL3ZpYmUtY2hlY2svZ3B0LTUtNSIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjoyMX0= or Opus 4.8 https://every., smart models that require specific instructions and careful prompting for the best results.

Instead, Fable 5 feels like working with a capable coworker—at least that’s Every’s consensus after a week of testing https://every..

“It feels like you have an engineer on your team that you just gave a problem to, and they’ll figure it out,” says Cora https://every.to/emails/click/136f006095268802530f927779a5f4d55a493840c0f1f77c950761a77b64df9e/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSG93IHRvIEdldCB0aGUgTW9zdCBPdXQgb2YgRmFibGUgNSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQyOTQsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2NvcmEuY29tcHV0ZXIvIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjI0fQ== general manager Kieran Klaassen https://every.to/emails/click/136f006095268802530f927779a5f4d55a493840c0f1f77c950761a77b64df9e/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSG93IHRvIEdldCB0aGUgTW9zdCBPdXQgb2YgRmFibGUgNSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQyOTQsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BraWVyYW5fMTM1NSIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjoyNX0=.

That means, to get the most out of Anthropic’s first Mythos-class model https://every. available to the public, you have to think like a manager https://every.: Equip the model with context, goals, and a way to verify the work, then step aside. It may even stumble on a solution you hadn’t considered.

Not every task deserves this treatment. Smart colleagues don’t come cheap, and neither does Fable 5. Here’s how to get the most out of this powerful new model and some of the workflows the team is using.
